clue.text: No white water activity here then?

definitions.text: No white water activity here then?

parts.words: No white water activity here then?
parts.note: a sea named for the colour opposite to white is jokingly offered as a place where white-water rafting could never happen

explanation.surface: A rafter wonders whether a place has no rapids worth running.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke turns the colour in the sea's name into the opposite of the foam of rapids, so this body of water hints itself.

clue.text: Hard homme de lettres climbing a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, so the writer's name runs backwards

parts.note: Albert Camus, the French writer, is a man of letters
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tough French writer shins up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses the French writer's surname because in a down entry the letters go upwards; 'Hard' joins at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The sumach is a small tree or shrub of the cashew family, grown for its foliage and spice.

clue.text: It provides suits for lawyers at hearing no call

parts.note: barristers collectively are the Bar

indicators.note: no here asks for a synonym of call to be dropped from the word beside it

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: Something supplies outfits to lawyers attending a hearing without a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes RING from HEARING, leaving HEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine woollen cloth used for suits and uniforms, so it provides suits.

clue.text: Primates pass on black magic

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
obi (obeah) is a form of West Indian sorcery

explanation.surface: Apes pass on dark sorcery.
explanation.definitionFit: Colobi are African colobus monkeys, which are primates.

clue.text: Exert a force over the opinion seeker

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to exert a force is to pull
G is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: Someone presses a pollster hard.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gallup founded the famous opinion poll, so his name stands for a seeker of public opinion.

clue.text: Celebrities en masse? Heavens above!

definitions.meaning: a gathering of stars, as in a glittering crowd of famous people
a vast system of stars in the sky

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a glittering assembly of famous people and a huge system of stars overhead.

clue.text: Jumbo pilot turning radio operator away

indicators.note: turning means the word for a radio amateur is reversed

parts.note: a ham is an amateur radio operator
out means away, as not at home

explanation.surface: A pilot of a jumbo jet turns away a radio operator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes MAH from HAM. 'Jumbo' is an elephant here, not a jet.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahout is an elephant driver, and Jumbo was a famous elephant.

clue.text: But did he made hay with his bombers?

definitions.text: But did he made hay with his bombers?

parts.words: But did he made hay with his bombers?
parts.note: names an RAF commander of bombers in the Second World War whose surname is also a farm machine that spreads hay to dry

explanation.surface: A wartime air chief is asked whether his bombers helped with haymaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Tedder commanded Allied air forces in the Second World War; a tedder is also a machine that turns hay.
explanation.definitionFit: The air marshal's name doubles as the machine that shakes out mown hay, hence the haymaking joke.

clue.text: Smashing Gatso TV, lush driven to note the 16s was he?

definitions.text: driven to note the 16s was he?

indicators.note: smashing breaks these words into pieces to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk breaks a speed camera and a television, then is driven to write music.
explanation.walkthrough: A Gatso is a British speed camera. 16 is PLANET: the composer wrote The Planets suite.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst composed The Planets, so he was driven to set those worlds to music.

clue.text: Girl amusing G-man and other agents

parts.note: Ali G is a comic character played by Sacha Baron Cohen
the CIA is the US intelligence agency, other agents from the FBI G-men

explanation.surface: A girl entertains an FBI man and other spies.
explanation.walkthrough: G-man suggests the FBI, but here it is the comedian's character Ali G.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicia is a female given name, a form of Alice, so the bare word girl stands for it by example.

clue.text: One about to leave a French concert with a soft-pedal

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: to leave asks for the abbreviation of about to go out of the word for concert

parts.note: accord means concert, agreement
C, for circa, means about
a means one

explanation.surface: A soloist is about to walk out of a French concert, piano damped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes C out of ACCORD, giving ACORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Una corda, literally one string, is the musical direction to play using the soft pedal.

clue.text: Alliance following a boundary reversion

indicators.note: following places the turned boundary after the letter A
reversion means turning back, so the cricket boundary is read backwards

parts.note: a six is a boundary hit in cricket

explanation.surface: An alliance is struck after a border is reverted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversion' makes XIS from SIX. In cricket, hitting the ball over the boundary scores six.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the Second World War alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan.

clue.text: One thumbing through the guide to the 5 down?

definitions.text: One thumbing through the guide to the 5 down?

parts.words: One thumbing through the guide to the 5 down?
parts.note: evokes Douglas Adams's comic novel about a guide to the stars, read as someone thumbing lifts

explanation.surface: Someone flicks through a guidebook to the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down is GALAXY: the clue alludes to The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, and 'thumbing' means asking for a lift, not turning pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller who thumbs lifts is the hero of the famous guide to the cosmos.

clue.text: Politician and dramatist have left following holiday, carrying the can

indicators.note: carrying links the holiday to the lavatory it brings along behind it

parts.note: vac is short for vacation
can is slang for lavatory, short lav
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has left on holiday and taken the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying the can' means taking the blame, but here 'the can' is a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaclav Havel was a Czech playwright who became president, both a politician and dramatist.

clue.text: Left one at Ironbridge with time to draw breath

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron and a span is a bridge

explanation.surface: Someone left at Ironbridge has time for a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironbridge is a Shropshire town famed for its iron bridge; here it splits into iron and bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifespan is the whole time a creature is alive and breathing.

clue.text: So seeing agreement in confrontation

definitions.meaning: people who see this way are in full agreement

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase completes the idiom for agreeing and also means facing each other directly.

clue.text: Chart alien from whence he came?

parts.note: to plan is to chart
ET is the film alien

explanation.surface: A map shows where an alien came from.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien comes from another world, so his place of origin is a heavenly body.

clue.text: King with a mole under one arm

parts.note: R, for rex, is king
a mole is a stone breakwater or pier

explanation.surface: A king has a mole under his arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' is a harbour wall, not the animal or the skin blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender sword, an arm in the sense of a weapon.

clue.text: Two sources of light water emergency

parts.note: a flash gives light
a flood, short for floodlight, gives light

explanation.surface: Two lamps go out in a burst pipe crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash flood is a sudden torrent of water, an emergency.

clue.text: Split in Brunelleschi's masterpiece

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A crack appears in the famous dome by the Florentine architect.
explanation.walkthrough: Brunelleschi built the dome of Florence cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split, especially within a church.

clue.text: Fight shy of English for "shy"

parts.note: to demur is to hesitate or object to something

explanation.surface: A writer hesitates to use an English word for timid.
explanation.definitionFit: Demure means modest and reserved, close to shy.

clue.text: No young shaver, this biblical twin?

definitions.text: No young shaver, this biblical twin?

parts.words: No young shaver, this biblical twin?
parts.note: points to the hairy twin brother of Jacob in Genesis, who would never have shaved

explanation.surface: A boy who never shaved is described as a twin from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young shaver' is slang for a boy; Genesis calls Esau a hairy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau, the elder twin of Jacob, was famously hairy, so no shaver.

clue.text: Flora's 14 has sent one mad

indicators.note: mad suggests letters thrown into disorder

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A plant's lifespan sends someone crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is LIFESPAN: anthesis is the flowering period, a flower's life stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthesis is the period when a flower is fully open, a span in a plant's life.

clue.text: Bunthorne's first work accepted on sight, with difficulty

parts.note: the setter's, so my
op. 1, opus one, is a composer's first work
A marked on a bill means accepted

explanation.surface: The setter's debut piece was accepted at first glance, though with trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunthorne is the setter, so his own possessions are MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is short-sightedness, sight that works only with difficulty.

clue.text: He discovered New Zealand since breaking timepiece

indicators.note: breaking means the word for since splits the other pieces

parts.note: T is time, and a man is a piece in chess or draughts
as means since

explanation.surface: An explorer reached New Zealand because his clock broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timepiece' looks like a clock but splits into time and piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel Tasman was the Dutch navigator who first sighted New Zealand in 1642.

clue.text: Collect one's suit

definitions.meaning: a collect is a short ... in church liturgy
a suit is a petition or entreaty

explanation.definitionFit: A collect is a short liturgical prayer, and a suit is a plea or petition.
